text.p: The dollar closed an uneventful European session barely changed as forex dealers stayed squarely focused on the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.

Robust U.S. consumer confidence data for September provided more ammunition for the hawkish FOMC members likely to argue for a rate rise, analysts said. U.S. Treasuries fell on the strong report but the dollar showed no marked response.
"This report clearly provides more evidence for the hawks to justify their call for a rate hike today," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at BankAmerica.
Consumer confidence was well above expectations at 118.8, compared with 107.00 forecast and 112.00 in Augst.
Dealers said the dollar's response to the FOMC meeting would depend on how the decision was explained to the market.
A rate hike sold as economic fine tuning would soothe markets, while a poorly-explained rise which suggested more tightening was in store would hit asset markets and the dollar.
Any annoucement from the FOMC will be around 1815 GMT after European markets have closed.
The dollar was at 1.5124/28 marks and 109.70/75 yen by 1426 GMT compared with 1.5118/28 and 109.82/92 in late Europe Monday.
A quarter-point rise in the federal funds target rate is largely discounted, but analysts are deeply divided over whether the FOMC will sanction a change in U.S. monetary policy at all.

The reaction of U.S. bond and stock markets is likely to prove crucial for the dollar, although the currency might find its upside limited if the Fed tightened by 25 basis points since that was already largely anticipated, analysts said.
Even if rates stay unchanged now, many economists feel the market will anticipate a move at the next meeting in November.
